text: Welcome, everybody. Thank you for joining. My name is Hannes Werten and I'm the main organizer and moderator of this online event on digital humanism informatics in times of COVID-19. It's somehow funny to make it online because I know there are many out there listening to us, but they just see the screen and the camera. We have in the program, we have eight renowned speakers and two co-moderators. Thanks to all of you for joining us and for doing and making this event possible. The program in short is just, we could say we're going from the digital human to politics in the program and from informatics to democracy. The first one, digital human to politics, is the first and the fourth block, the last block. And informatics to democracy is the second and the third block. So I think we have a nice parenthesis. As a background and the reason for this, the crisis shows that informatics is essential. It keeps the system running. It's really something like the operating system of our society and economy, as also Moshe Wade is phrasing it. But we also have critical issues related to democracy, to privacy, to security, fake news and things. And that's what digital humanism is about. It's dealing with the complex relationship and interplay of humans and machines and the co-evolution that we will hear something about that later. I also would like to thank the supporters. like the Digital Enlightenment Forum in Brussels, IEEE, Informatics Europe, the Vienna Science and Technology Fund, and the Faculty of Informatics of TU Wien. The support is not a financial one. It's more a moral one, an organizational one, and a content-related one. I think the most important things are the organizational and technical issues. And I have to confess, when we were organizing this event, it seems to be more work to organize an online event than to do a physical conference. It has to be planned very exactly. We will have each speaker with 15 to 20 minutes and then a Q&A session. So for each speaker, more or less 30 minutes. And I really ask you to keep this timing. The participants who have registered, they have to raise their hand and then they are activated by the moderator and then they can speak. Or they can also use the Q&A button. I just ask you to tell your name, who you are, and then try to keep it short. Also on YouTube, you could. Use the Q&A.
